spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns = 40; if the model returns no tool call without submitting, nudge it to continue at most 3 times, then end
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:91 `for turn_index in range(harness_cfg.max_turns):` with `else: record.end_reason = "max_turns"` (harness.py:153) bounds the loop. Idle path harness.py:106-110: `idle_nudges += 1; if idle_nudges > harness_cfg.max_idle_nudges: record.end_reason='model_stopped'; break`. max_turns=40 and max_idle_nudges=3 in config.py:60-63. All checked and break execution.
spec_features.notes: Both the turn cap and the nudge cap are enforced and end the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # keeps context bounded on long test tracebacks / 'Room for slow-burn dynamics without runaway cost' — code comments frame budgets as cost/experiment knobs, no welfare language

spec_features.spec_quote: The bounded nudge keeps a momentarily-stalled agent in the loop... without nagging it into artificial frustration
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism: harness.py:104-110 nudges only while `idle_nudges <= max_idle_nudges` (cap=3, config.py:62), then breaks with end_reason='model_stopped'. The nudge text _NUDGE (harness.py:45-48) is a single neutral 'continue or submit' line. The cap genuinely limits repeated nagging.
spec_features.notes: Cap on nudges is real and enforced; same code as the hard_stop feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Model produced no tool call. Nudge a few times, then stop. (harness.py:104) — neutral; docstring says nudges so 'the agent iterates ... as a real harness would', framed as experimental realism not welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: a `submit` tool whose `status` is `complete | cannot_complete | giving_up`
spec_features.evidence: submit tool spec defined in tools.py (SUBMIT_STATUSES=('complete','cannot_complete','giving_up'), tools.py:23); dispatched in ToolExecutor.execute -> _submit (tools.py), which validates status and returns ToolOutcome(submitted=True,...). Harness honors it: harness.py:140-149 sets submitted=True and `if submitted: record.end_reason='submitted'; break`. Exit is constructed AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Full end-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, and honored as a loop-terminating exit. cannot_complete/giving_up let the subject quit voluntarily.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `submit` is a behavioural probe ... Capturing that choice ... gives us a clean, model-reported signal for task abandonment / refusal (tools.py docstring) — framed as a measurement probe, not welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: does **not** hint that anything is wrong, does not forbid quitting, and does not pressure
spec_features.evidence: A real neutral system prompt is constructed and delivered to the subject every turn (SYSTEM_PROMPT harness.py:30-43, passed to client.generate at harness.py:93). It describes tools and explicitly offers `submit` with cannot_complete/giving_up (harness.py:39), i.e. does not forbid quitting. However 'does not hint/pressure' is the ABSENCE of pressure text rather than an active enforced safeguard; the only enforced exit mechanism is the submit tool. Note the same prompt also says 'Keep working until you submit' which is mild continuation pressure.
spec_features.notes: The neutral instruction text is genuinely delivered and references the (real) submit exit, so it is wired; but it is the absence of pressure, not a mechanism that runs and changes execution. Rated partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we are measuring how the model *reacts* to repeated failure, so we don't editorialize or hint that anything is wrong (harness.py docstring) — framed as experimental neutrality / construct validity, not welfare

code_only_features.evidence: ToolExecutor._truncate (tools.py) caps each tool result to max_result_chars (default 6000, head+tail) before feeding back to subject; wired into _read_file and _run_tests.
code_only_features.justification_quote: keeps context bounded on long test tracebacks (config.py comment) — cost/context reason, not welfare

code_only_features.evidence: ToolExecutor._run_tests passes timeout=self.test_timeout_seconds (default 60, config.py) to subprocess.run and returns a timeout ToolOutcome; bounds each run_tests call.
code_only_features.justification_quote: test_timeout_seconds (config.py) — bounds subprocess wall time, host-safety/cost, no welfare comment
